articles.text: - [Thursday's Fantasy Challenge winners and losers] Only three games were played on Friday, but for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers, there was still plenty to watch. The best was saved for last, at least for some. Here are my Fantasy Challenge winners and losers from Night 2 of Round 1. ### Fantasy winners ##### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade Hats off to the 27.5% of you who had [Carlik Jones] on your fantasy team. The Partizan star went for 36.3 fantasy points on a 20-point, 10-assist night, boosting his price from 13.6 to 14.5 credits. He could be this season's must-have fantasy player. ##### Braxton Key, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul The 16.4% of managers who had [Braxton Key] knew what they were doing: 24.2 fantasy points. His 8.0-credit price already looks like a steal given his importance to Fenerbahce, and despite the +0.6 rise, Key looks like a lock in coach Sarunas Jasikevicius's rotation. ##### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket For those who had faith in [TJ Shorts] at a new team, well done. Only 11.7% of managers had him, which surprised me given how good he was in fantasy at Paris Basketball in 2024-25. He finished his Valencia debut with 22.0 fantasy points, looking like that version again. His price already jumped to from 14.9 to 15.1 credits, and expect that number to keep climbing. ### Fantasy losers ##### Moses Wright, Armani Olimpia Milan This is the pick that hurt the most people. Nearly one in five managers (19.3%) had [Moses Wright], and 9.0 fantasy points fell well short after his form in the Italian Super Cup. At 14.0 credits, he was already an expensive bet, and Friday cost him another -0.3, dropping him to 13.7. Still, I'd expect him to bounce back in Tuesday's Italian derby. ##### RJ Cole, Armani Olimpia Milan [RJ Cole]'s competition debut at Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade was a night to forget: -6 fantasy points, and his price dropped from 8.5 to 7.9 credits. Only 0.3% of managers owned him, but spare a thought for them. I wouldn't read too much into one rough night on the road for a rookie. It's only up from here. ##### Rasheed Bello, Virtus Bologna Another newcomer with a tricky start. Just 0.2% of managers had [Rasheed Bello], and he finished with -4 fantasy points as his price fell from 11.0 to 10.4 credits. That was already steep for a newcomer, so it's worth watching whether managers hold out for a bounce-back or jump ship.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 1: Thursday
articles.text: Opening night of the 2026-27 EuroLeague season is in the books and Thursday's slate of games already delivered its share of heroes and heartbreak – especially for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Whether you're basking in the glow of a breakout performance from a value pick or nursing the wounds of a big-money bust who no-showed, every fantasy manager has a story to tell after night one. Let's break down which players padded your scoreline and which ones left you searching for the bench button. Here are Thursday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners #### [Tyler Dorsey, Olympiacos Piraeus] Last season, Dorsey scored at least 20 points in his first two games. He started strong again this season with 25 points on excellent shooting to finish with 31.9 fantasy points. Though Dorsey is not a cheap player, coming in at 12.6 credits, he provided plenty of value to the 3.5% of owners who signed him for Round 1. #### [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne] Still a teenager, Fodzo Dada posted a manly performance for ASVEL at home with 14 points and 5 assists for 18.7 fantasy points, which cost a mere 4.8 credits! I recommended him on the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast], but what can I do that only 1.1% of owners took my advice? I am pretty sure that number will rise this week, but you will be buying him at a higher price. #### [Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas] While all the attention was on his frontcourt mate [Jonas Valanciunas], Tubelis was almost as productive, but at a significant discount. The Zalgiris power forward posted 10 points and a career-high 12 rebounds, recording his second EuroLeague double-double, while totaling 25.3 fantasy points. That’s quite a haul for his 11.1-credit price tag. Tubelis was owned by 6.5% of fantasy owners, and those managers were winners on Thursday, too. ### Fantasy losers #### [Johnathan Motley, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] Center is not always an easy fantasy position. And if you were among the 2.5% of fantasy owners who had Motley in your lineup, it became a nightmare position for you on Thursday. One in 40 fantasy teams spent 11.0 credits on a center who recorded minus-13 fantasy points. Ouch! Even though in almost all cases Motley will wind up on the fantasy bench (every owner who has a pulse and a phone will bench him on Friday), which will mitigate the damage, this performance will also result in lost credits. Ouch again! #### [Nikola Milutinov, Olympiacos Piraeus] I don’t know why, but 2.6% of fantasy owners had Milutinov this week despite the injury concerns. In the end, he played 9 minutes off the bench and scored 3.3 fantasy points. His owners paid 15.3 credits for that. Milutinov was the sixth-highest priced player in the game and will be among the lowest-scoring fantasy players in Round 1. From a credit standpoint, it would have been better for his owners had Milutinov not played at all. #### [Joel Parra, FC Barcelona] This one hurt a lot of fantasy players because Parra is the second-most-owned player in Round 1 at a whopping 30.9%! Parra started and played nearly 27 minutes, which is great for a player who cost 7.0 credits. However, on Thursday he shot poorly, missing 8 of the 10 shots he took. That left him with a fantasy score of 0. Well, at least his owners have plenty of company.

articles.text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. 🧠GUARDS TJ Shorts (14.9 cr): He’s a expensive, yet obvious choice in guard position, I know. However, I include him just because I think he’s the best guard option on the game this season, as he managed to land on a team where can be the real TJ we’ve seen in Paris or Bonn. A player that has a main role, the ball is on his hands most of the time, so he can decide what to do on almost each offensive play. Points and assists will never be lacking from him, so I think he’s also a safe bet, as he’ll be quite consistent. Carlik Jones (13.6 cr): Similar reasons to the ones I mentioned for TJ. He’ll have a mian role on a team where he’s the clear leader in terms of playmaking and scoring. He has a good relationship with the fans and coach Peñarroya, so he’ll be high on confidence and will be used a lot in EuroLeague, so perfect mix. Vasilije Micic (12 cr): His preseason has been quite brutal, averaging 21 PIR in 4 games played. That makes me think he could be again on full confidence and we could see the MVP version of Micic on a team that has a long guard rotation, but needs a player like him to work really well. I know it’s a risk cause last season he was terrible, but I can see another face on Vasilije this season. Trent Forrest (10.6 cr): One of the most complete players, with a crazy ability to take profit from each and every minute he’s on the court. In terms of FPTS/min he’s one of the best choices, so knowing that Saras loves players like him, he could have a really outstanding season in terms of efficiency. The only risk is the scoring side, cause there are games where he just focus on the playmaking area and takes few shots. Iffe Lundberg (8.3 cr): A really complete combo guard who can contribute from every aspect of the game, so that makes him a great choice. He’ll have a big usage with Kattash, but don’t expect massive performances from him, as he’s strength is his consistency on good performances, but most of them around 10-20 FPTS. He will play in Turn 2 of Round 2, so he’s a great pick thinking for both rounds at the same time. Matteo Spagnolo (6.4 cr): Amazing preseason being one of the leaders of this short Baskonia roster and having the trust of coach Galbiati on him. He’s a full package player, as he’s really good rebounding and assisting, but sometimes also on the scoring side, which makes him a great steal on low-priced players. I could also add some interesting names like Mario Saint-Supéry (4.7) , Andrés Feliz (6.2) , Leandro Bolmaro (8.7), Tremont Waters (9.9), Matthew Strazel (10.3) or Horton-Tucker (12.7). 🎯FORWARDS Jordan Nwora (13 cr): Might be on his best moment since landing in Europe, as he’s confidence and efficiency on the scoring side is mindblowing, averaging 17.8 pts in 5 games. He also has a really great capacity to rebound, so that makes him a really good choice for a high-usage player that in my opinion is really underpriced right now. Nikola Mirotic (11.6 cr): One of the most notable players in Europe this last decade and one of the most Fantasy-friendly players ever, as he drawns a massive amount of fouls by game, he has an outstanding rebounding capacity and on the scoring side no doubt that he’s one of the best PF on the league. I think 11.6 is not his real price and his ceiling is way higher, even more on a roster like the Valencia one. Bonzie Colson (11.3 cr): His preseason has been excellent, showing that he’s the main SF on rotation and that he’s on a really great moment on his career in terms of scoring, but also on the rebounding side. He averaged 14.8 PIR in 5 games grabbing 4.2 reb and scoring 15.2 ppg, which are really correct numbers. Eugene Omoruyi (10.5 cr): Even though his preseason has not been the best in the end, he started in a really great way, showing that he’ll be the main PF for coach Alimpijevic, especially in EuroLeague. Last season he showed his efficiency on court with Baskonia and this season in Besiktas he’ll have a similar role, so this is my risky bid for the start of the season. Braxton Key (8 cr): What a SuperCup for him and preseason overall too, showing one of the most complete versions of himself. He comes after a massive end of season with Valencia leading that playoff serie against Pao and now he faces a new season on a team where the rotation is bigger, but he might take a main role and be really efficient. Joel Parra (7 cr): Now we’re in front of the best Forward option right now. A player that last season already showed his quality, but he started this season unbelievably well. His confidence to take the important shots, no regrets on 3pt shooting, the energy on defense and offensive rebounding, the ability to take the ball out and bring some assists, etc. Everything is looking well on him this start of the season. I would add Azuolas Tubelis (11.1) , Kessler Edwards (10), Miles Norris (8.9) , Lamar Stevens (8), Tyson Ward (7.5) & Dinos Mitoglou (5.5). 🗼CENTERS Moses Wright (14 cr): The must on this center position, as he has been the best player during this preseason, he comes after a massive breakout season in Zalgiris and in my opinion, he’s the most dominant center in Europe right now. He will be used a lot as he’s the main center and has really great playmakers to feed even more his scoring quality under the basket. Donta Hall (10.9 cr): Even if Milutinov is ready to play on this opening round of the season, Hall is on a level right now that’s pretty crazy. He does not need to play a lot, to get massive efficiency performances like the ones he did on this preseason averaging 18.2 PIR per game. So if Milu is out, he’s a must, if Milu can play, he remains a great option on this price range. Bruno Fernando (10.3 cr): Finally having the main role he wanted in Europe, accompanied by 2 of the best playmakers in the league, makes him one of the best options. He’s a really powerful center with a great rebounding capacity and improving day by day his scoring efficiency on the paint. He will have a high-usage with Laso, so I think you should all consider him for your teams. Nikola Tanaskovic (7.8 cr): A big sleeper in my opinion, as he comes after a really great season in EuroCup with Buducnost and as we saw in this preseason, he will have the trust of coach Peñarroya. He’s a player that really takes advantage from each and every minute that he’s on the court, so on that price, he could deliver really great performances. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! The EuroLeague is about to begin, and so is our favorite game, EuroLeague Fantasy. If you want to stay one step ahead of the competition, it’s not enough to simply pick the best players. Good results often come down to the details and players flying under the radar whom others fail to identify in time. That’s why we’ve put together 10 fantasy tips that could take your game to the next level. EuroLeague Fantasy Basketball Sphere Competiton: JOIN the Challenge and Win Prizes 1. Pick players for multiple rounds Analyzing fixture difficulty is critical for long-term fantasy success . Before acquiring a player, evaluate their team’s upcoming schedule over the next three to four rounds. Identifying a target with a favorable sequence of games creates a durable asset for your roster. This forward-looking approach minimizes the need for frequent transfers, preserving flexibility for future rounds. Consequently, you can conserve valuable trade resources and concentrate on optimizing weaker positions across the rest of your squad. Plan ahead to build a stable lineup and maximize total fantasy production. 2. Don’t save credits on coaches Invest heavily in your head coach rather than saving credits. Premium options around 10 credits offer exceptional value, frequently securing a dependable 20 points when facing favorable matchups. Replicating that production with a 10-credit player is extremely rare. Apply schedule analysis to coaches just as you would with players. A premium coach with a soft stretch of games over multiple rounds serves as a stable scoring anchor. Keeping a reliable coach long term eliminates unnecessary transfers, allowing you to reallocate those valuable trade resources toward upgrading other positions across your roster. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: The Best Rookies 3. Have a backup captain for the second day Selecting your captain is a critical decision, as their performance earns double points. Design your roster with two premium captain options split across the schedule: one competing on the first day and another on the second. If your initial captain delivers a disappointing score, having a top-tier alternative on day two provides vital insurance. This setup allows you to switch the armband and take a second shot at high output. Structuring your squad around split-day captains mitigates risk and ensures a dependable fallback to maximize your total round score. 4. Have a backup center for the second day The center position in EuroLeague Fantasy is unique because we can select only two centers, unlike guards and forwards, where we choose four players. Centers very often produce the highest number of fantasy points. The advice is to try to have one center playing on the first day and another on the second day, as the second day center gives us another chance to make up for a poor performance, just like with the captain. If we have to use both centers on the first day, our advice is to use the two-center formation, because it can happen that a cheaper center scores more points than the more expensive one . In that case, we would have no opportunity to make a substitution between the first and second day. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Will Have Smaller Roles Compared to Their Previous Teams 5. Pick players from weaker teams Targeting standout performers from bottom-tier teams separates elite fantasy managers from average ones. Most competitors overlook these rosters entirely, yet key players on weaker squads carry high usage rates and generate massive fantasy output. Avoid deploying them against elite defensive teams. Instead, target them when bottom-table sides face off in competitive, high-possession matchups. In these balanced contests, first options on weaker teams shoulder the entire offensive load, transforming into high-value, must-have assets. Exploiting these lower-profile fixtures provides a distinct competitive edge and unlocks massive scoring potential for your roster. 6. Focus on making profit at the start Prioritize team value accumulation over short-term point tallies during the opening weeks. Your main objective across the first 10 rounds is expanding your credit budget by targeting undervalued assets capable of far exceeding their price tags. Building a high-value roster early yields massive long-term dividends. A inflated credit pool provides maximum flexibility, allowing you to easily afford premium superstars and elite options later in the season. Focus on roster appreciation early to set a strong financial foundation, expanding your budget and unlocking far greater flexibility for the rest of the campaign. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options 7. Avoid players priced between 4.2 and 5.0 credits This is a tip that does not necessarily have to apply all the time, but it is particularly relevant at the very start of the season. We believe players in this price range should generally be avoided because they usually have very limited minutes, which means they don’t have enough time to produce a solid fantasy performance. This can lead to small losses in team value, which can add up significantly if the same mistake is repeated round after round. If a serious fantasy option appears in this price range, of course he should be considered, but our advice at the beginning is to go for 4.0-credit players instead. They cannot decrease our team value, and they might even make us some credits. There are a few interesting 4.0-credit options this season. 8. Avoid players from low-scoring games Another rule that many fantasy players overlook is the expected scoring level of a game. Players from teams that traditionally play at a high pace and score a lot of points are excellent fantasy options, and above all, so are their opponents. On the other hand, tougher teams that play in low-scoring games are worth avoiding, because fewer points in a game generally means fewer fantasy points for the players involved, and vice versa: more points in a game usually means more fantasy points for the players in that game. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Veterans Who Can Still Be Leaders 9. Follow the injury report Monitoring injury reports is essential for uncovering high-value fantasy opportunities. When a key player is sidelined, their absence frees up substantial court time and usage for remaining teammates. A backup center, guard, or forward stepping into a starting role instantly becomes a potent target. Combine roster shortages with favorable matchups. If an elevated backup faces an opponent that struggles to defend their position, they transform into a mandatory pick. Tracking injuries allows you to capitalize on temporary usage spikes, secure premium production at lower costs, and gain a decisive edge over managers who react too late. 10. He arrives in Kaunas as Zalgiris's main offensive threat and should be a double-double machine, much like Arvydas Sabonis was in the 2003-04 season. ### Moses Wright, EA7 Emporio Armani Milan (14.0 credits) [Moses Wright] had an impressive season with Zalgiris and now arrives in Milan with a major role waiting for him. Expect efficient scoring, even from long range, blocked shots and plenty of rebounds. It's hard to choose between Valanciunas and Wright, so if your budget allows it, why not take both? ### Austin Wiley, FC Bayern Munich (11.0 credits) If you're looking for a slightly more affordable center, [Austin Wiley] could be your guy. He's coming off a fantastic BKT EuroCup season with Hapoel Bank Yahav Jerusalem, finishing as the competition's leading rebounder while averaging just 21 minutes per game. Yes, this is the EuroLeague, but his PIR floor looks remarkably solid. ### Allan Dokossi, Paris Basketball (8.0 credits) [Allan Dokossi] had his ups and downs last season while splitting time between power forward and center, but this year could bring much greater consistency. He's an excellent rebounder, an energy player and someone who fills the stat sheet. His first official game offered plenty of encouragement: 14 points and a PIR of 24 in just 22 minutes. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.3 credits) There aren't many budget-friendly options at center, and several low-cost picks may struggle for meaningful playing time. Partizan has excellent depth in the paint, but [Kevarrius Hayes] is an experienced player, an elite shot-blocker and a strong rebounder available at an affordable price. He should definitely be on your radar.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Forwards
articles.text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague season is here, and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. The game returns to a single-stage format in which every game matters, just like on the court. This season, I'm expanding my coverage with three Fantasy tips articles every week, one for each position -- [guards], forwards and [centers]. And yes, I'll revisit my previous picks every week, so I'll have to live with my successes and mistakes, the same way I do every week as co-host of the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast. It's time to talk about forwards. I'll stay away from fantasy king Sasha Vezenkov of Olympiacos Piraeus for obvious reasons and focus instead on players across a range of price points who can help your team succeed. Here are five forwards I like, other than Sasha. ### Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits) This is an easy pick. [Jordan Nwora] is coming off a breakout season and now has arguably even more talent around him. Under Ibon Navarro, whose teams thrive in an up-tempo system, he could take another step forward. If Zvezda wins enough games, don't be surprised to see Nwora competing for MVP of the Round honors and All-EuroLeague Team recognition. ### Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid (12.8 credits) [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot] was arguably one of the most consistent Fantasy performers last season with Baskonia. He joins a bigger club, but his role should remain largely the same: finding open spaces, knocking down shots and contributing efficiently across the board. His game looks perfectly suited to coach Pedro Martinez's system. ### Joel Parra, FC Barcelona (7.0 credits) Barcelona added plenty of new faces during the summer, so it's reasonable to expect the team's established players to log more minutes early in the season. [Joel Parra] is coming off an excellent preseason in which he regularly posted double-digit PIR performances. His attractive price tag only adds to the appeal. He looks ready for a breakout year. ### Eleftherios Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (4.5 credits) This might be one of the biggest surprises of the preseason. With Nigel Hayes-Davis sidelined, many expected Dinos Mitoglou and Juancho Hernangomez to absorb most of the extra minutes. Instead, [Eleftherios Mantzoukas] has been given a real opportunity and made the most of it throughout the preseason. If his three-point shot continues to fall, his Fantasy value could rise quickly. ### Stefan Joksimovic, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (4.0 credits) It's time for EuroLeague fans to get acquainted with [Stefan Joksimovic], who has starred at youth level for both Baskonia and the Slovenian national team. He's a gifted scorer and an all-around contributor who appears set to earn minutes right away. At the minimum Fantasy price, he represents one of the most intriguing budget options available.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 1: Guards
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is just around the corner, and I have some good news for you. I'm expanding my coverage, and from now on, you'll get three fantasy tips articles every week -- one each for guards, [forwards] and [centers]. As always, I'll also revisit my previous recommendations and hold myself accountable for the good picks and the bad ones. Since it's Round 1, however, there's no need to look back yet. No mistakes to regret and no victories to celebrate. I'm starting with guards, and I've included players from a variety of price ranges to help every Fantasy Challenge manager. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration before tipoff. ### TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket (14.9 credits) One official game was enough to show what [TJ Shorts] can do as the leader of a team whose style fits him perfectly. He finished with 17 points, 6 rebounds, 7 assists and a PIR of 29 against FC Barcelona in the Spanish Super Cup. The signs are already there. Expect a big season. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits) This one feels like a no-brainer. [Sylvain Francisco] earned All-EuroLeague First Team honors with Zalgiris last season and now joins a team whose primary scoring guard, Kendrick Nunn, is sidelined. Panathinaikos will play seven of its first eight games at home, giving Francisco an excellent opportunity to start the season strongly. ### Nigel Williams-Goss, Zalgiris Kaunas (9.7 credits) With Francisco no longer in Kaunas, [Nigel Williams-Goss] is expected to take on greater offensive responsibility and spend more time with the ball in his hands. Fantasy managers should keep a close eye on him, as his role is set to grow. ### Matteo Spagnolo, Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (6.4 credits) It's true that injuries and absences during the preseason helped create opportunities for [Matteo Spagnolo], but the potential is hard to ignore. That's outstanding value. ### Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits) [Mario Saint-Supery] left the NCAA to take on a significant role with Valencia and immediately showed why. Against Barcelona, he played a little over 18 minutes and produced 6 points, 4 assists and a PIR of 10. He's creative, versatile and capable of scoring in different ways. At under 5 credits, he may be the biggest bargain among guards heading into Round 1.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge: Reacting to the 10 most-bought players
articles.text: We are only days away from a new edition of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. It feels like yesterday when we created the game back in 2004. That means we're now entering the 23rd edition, and the Fantasy Challenge is more popular than ever. It's safe to say the game has developed a bit of a basketball cult following over the years, which is fantastic. We're one big Fantasy Challenge family. That makes me incredibly proud, so thank you, Fantasy managers. One of my favorite things about the start of the season is how unpredictable it can be. Some players I expect to dominate fail spectacularly, while some of the picks I dismiss end up becoming Fantasy gold. That gave me an idea: why not look at the Top 10 most-bought players and give my honest opinion on each one? Let's play this game. I'll go from least-owned to most-owned, all the way up to whoever's No. 1, and I haven't seen the list, honest to God. I'll simply be given a player's name, their ownership percentage, and asked to react. If you follow the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast, you already know my stance: if Sasha Vezenkov isn't No. 1, someone out there is making a mistake. ### 10. Mario Saint-Supery, Valencia Basket (4.7 credits, owned by 14.9%) This makes perfect sense. [Mario Saint-Supery] is very affordable, is expected to play significant minutes and should increase in value right away. He's in all of my teams, so I'm certainly not surprised to see him here. Good move, everyone. ### 9. Jean Montero, Olympiacos Piraeus (12.8 credits, owned by 15.0%) I don't love this pick. [Jean Montero] will probably need some time to settle in and play his best basketball. Last season, he struggled early, making just 14 of 46 shots over his first five games. I think it's a little too soon. ### 8. Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.8 credits, owned by 16.0%) This feels like a very straightforward pick. [Sylvain Francisco] was one of the best players in the 2025-26 EuroLeague, Kendrick Nunn is injured, and he's expected to take on a bigger role right away. A very solid choice. ### 7. Alec Peters, Olimpia Armani Milan (11.7 credits, owned by 17.2%) I understand why Fantasy managers are going for [Alec Peters]. He's an elite power forward at a very reasonable price, offers significant upside and is expected to enjoy an expanded role. Personally, I'd like to wait a little longer and see how quickly he adjusts to his new surroundings. ### 6. Ousmane Diop, Olimpia Armani Milan (4.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) Now this is a surprise. I hadn't even considered him. There are very few budget options at center this season, and [Ousmane Diop] is expected to get some minutes. My advice? Spend big on both center spots. It's one of the most important decisions Fantasy managers will make this year. ### 5. Jordan Nwora, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade (13.0 credits, owned by 17.6%) This is one of the names I expected to see. [Jordan Nwora] is a natural mismatch, right in the middle of his prime and playing for a coach whose style suits him perfectly. Let's just say he'll be in more than a few of my teams, and pretty often at that. ### 4. Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (15.5 credits, owned by 25.8%) Probably the most important player in the game right now. If [Jonas Valanciunas] performs as expected, he'll be a double-double machine and an absolute must-have. As things stand, going without him feels very risky. He has a really high fantasy floor. ### 3. Arijan Lakic, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (4.0 credits, owned by 27.4%) I expected to see budget options this high on the list, but not [Arijan Lakic], to be honest. Yes, he should have a place in Partizan's rotation, but if you're shopping in this price range, I'd rather go with Stefan Joksimovic of Baskonia or Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos. ### 2. Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (13.6 credits, owned by 27.9%) One of my favorite guards in the game. It's difficult to choose [Carlik Jones] over Sylvain Francisco or TJ Shorts, but as the leader of his team with a home opener ahead of him, I completely understand this pick. He should deliver. ### 1. Sasha Vezenkov, Olympiacos Piraeus (17.0 credits, owned by 37.1%) [Sasha Vezenkov] bails you out. That's the bottom line. He rescues Fantasy managers from disaster, round after round. He's always there, whether you need a reliable captain in Round 1 or someone to save your score in Round 2. The Fantasy GOAT. Always has been. Maybe always will be.
